data.long_meaning: From the Georgian language, Giorgi means 'farmer' or 'earthworker'. In Greek, it is derived from 'Georgios', meaning 'earthworker' or 'farmer'. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Giorgi usually hope their child will grow to embody farmer, earthworker and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Γεώργιος προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'γη' (γη) που σημαίνει 'γη' ή 'εδάφος' και 'έργον' (εργον) που σημαίνει 'εργασία' ή 'καλλιέργεια'. in_latin.name: Georgius

It is derived from the Greek words 'γη' (gē) 'earth' or 'soil' and 'έργον' (ergon) 'work' or 'labor'. The name became popular in Europe during the Middle Ages due to its association with Saint George, a prominent Christian martyr and saint. Giorgi symbolizes the Christian ideal of a devoted servant of God, reflecting virtues of hard work and dedication.
